items.stem: 党的十九大报告指出，我国经济已由（）阶段转向（）阶段，正处于转变发展方式、优化经济结构、转换增长动力的攻关期，建设现代化经济体系是跨越关口的迫切要求和我国发展的战略目标。

items.explanation: 供给学派着重分析税制对生产要素供给和利用的效果，他们指出，经济主体从事经营活动所关心的并不是获得的报酬或利润总额，而是减去各种纳税后的报酬或利润净额。在累进税制条件下，边际税率是关键因素，因为经济主体是否多做工作，或增加储蓄和投资，要看按边际税率纳税后增加的净报酬是否合算。供给学派经济政策的核心是减税。故选 B 项。

items.explanation: 根据边际效用递减规律，在一定时间内，在其他商品的消费数量保持不变的条件下，随着消费者对某种商品消费量的增加，消费者从该商品连续增加的每一消费单位中所得到的效用增量即边际效用是递减的。但只要边际效用大于零，总效用就是增加的。故选 B 项。

items.stem: A 公司是一家玩具生产企业，为防范生产的玩具给客户造成人身伤害或财产损失等风险，A 公司可以投保（）。
items.explanation:
产品责任保险是指以产品制造者、销售者、维修者等的产品责任为承保风险的一种责任保险，而产品责任又以各国的产品责任法律制度为基础。题中 A 公司以公司生产的产品的责任来投保，防范玩具给客户带来人身伤害或财产损失，符合产品责任保险的范畴。
公众责任保险又称普通责任保险或综合责任保险，它以被保险人的公众责任为承保对象，是责任保险中独立的、适用范围最为广泛的保险类别。所谓公众责任，是指致害人在公众活动场所的过错行为致使他人的人身或财产遭受损害，依法应由致害人承担的对受害人的经济赔偿责任。
雇主责任保险是指被保险人所雇用的员工在受雇过程中从事与保险单所载明的与被保险人业务有关的工作而遭受意外或患与业务有关的国家规定的职业性疾病，所致伤、残或死亡，被保险人根据《中华人民共和国劳动法》及劳动合同应承担的医药费用及经济赔偿责任，包括应支出的诉讼费用，由保险人在规定的赔偿限额内负责赔偿的一种保险。
职业责任保险亦称“职业赔偿保险”，承保专业技术人员因职业上的疏忽或过失致使合同对方或其他人遭受人身伤害或财产损失，依法应承担的赔偿责任。其承保对象，包括医生、会计师、建筑师、工程师、律师、保险经纪人、交易所经纪人与其他专业技术人员；一般由承保对象从事专业技术服务的单位投保。
故选 A 项。

items.stem: 下列关于资本的说法，正确的是（）。

options.A: 经济资本就是账面资本
options.B: 会计资本是监管部门规定的商业银行应持有的同其所承担的业务总体风险水平相匹配的资本

items.stem: 假设一家银行今年的税后收入是 200 万元，资产总额是 10 000 万元，所有者权益为 3 000 万元，则该银行的资产收益率（ROA）是（）。
items.explanation: 资产收益率是用来衡量每单位资产创造多少净利润的指标。其计算公式：资产收益率=$净利润\div平均资产总额\times 100\%$. 因此，该银行的资产收益率$200\div10000\times 100\%=2\%$. 故选A项。

items.explanation: 两全保险是指被保险人在保险合同约定的保险期间内死亡，或在保险期间届满仍生存时，保险人按照保险合同约定均应承担给付保险金责任的人寿保险。在两全保险中，当被保险人在保险期间内死亡时，保险人按合同约定将死亡保险金支付给受益人，保险合同终止；若被保险人生存至保险期间届满，保险人将生存保险金支付给被保险人。故选 B 项。

items.explanation:
狭义的表外业务一般包括以下三种类型：
（1）担保类业务。担保类业务是指商业银行接受客户的委托对第三方承担责任的业务，包括担保（保函）、备用信用证、跟单信用证、承兑等。

items.stem: 加强宏观审慎监管的必要性在于（）。

options.A: 金融创新过度导致系统性风险加大
options.B: 微观审慎监管对顺周期性无能为力
options.C: 金融全球化发展促使风险在全球范围内传递
options.D: 金融市场同质性加速金融市场不稳定性

items.explanation: 加强宏观审慎监管的必要性在于防范系统性金融风险，防止金融系统对经济体系的负外部溢出。具体来说，加强宏观审慎监管的必要性包括以下几点：（1）金融创新过度导致系统性风险加大；（2）微观审慎监管对顺周期性无能为力；（3）金融全球化发展促使风险在全球范围内传递；（4）金融市场同质性加速金融市场不稳定性；（5）建立健全宏观审慎政策框架；（6）强化逆周期管理；（7）提升重点机构和领域的稳健性；（8）控制金融体系的顺周期性和跨部门风险传染。通过这些措施，宏观审慎监管有助于提高金融体系的韧性和稳健性，降低金融危机发生的可能性和破坏性，促进金融体系的整体健康与稳定。故选 ABCD 项。

items.explanation: 保险中介是指介于保险经营机构之间或保险经营机构与投保人之间，专门从事保险业务咨询与销售、风险管理与安排、价值衡量与评估、损失鉴定与理算等中介服务活动，并从中依法获取佣金或手续费的单位或个人。保险中介人的主体形式多样，主要包括保险代理人、保险经纪人和保险公估人等。此外，一些其他专业领域的单位或个人也可以从事某些特定的保险中介服务，如保险精算师事务所、事故调查机构和律师等。故选 BCD 项。

items.source: 真题/【考试喵】2020年银保监会笔试真题及解析-财经岗.md
items.stem: It is indicated in the first paragraph that ___ .

options.A: the strength of high-speed trading firms is the computerization
options.B: the profits of high-speed trading are declining in recent years
options.C: all the high-speed firms are no longer profitable
options.D: every high-speed trader can make more money than the traditional traders

items.explanation: 主旨题。题目意为：第一段表明 ___ 。A 项，高速交易公司的优势在于计算机化；B 项，近年来高速交易的利润在下降；C 项，所有的高速公司都不再营利了；D 项，每一个高速交易者都能比传统交易者赚更多的钱。根据第一段中 “struggling” “down 35 percent from last year and 74 percent from the peak of two years ago” 可知，本段主要是说高速交易利润有所下降。故选 B 项。

items.source: 真题/【考试喵】2020年银保监会笔试真题及解析-财经岗.md
items.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, the decline of high-speed trading firms is characterized by ___ .

options.B: the shrink of stock trading market
options.C: the reduction of profits and employee numbers
options.D: no longer being active in the nation's stock market

items.explanation:
细节理解题。题目意为：根据前两段，高速交易公司衰落的特征是 ___ 。第一段主要说了高速交易的利润在下降，“Profits from high-speed trading in American stocks are reported to be, at most, $1.25 billion this year, down 35 percent from last year and 74 percent from the peak of two years ago, according to estimates from the brokerage firm Rosenblatt.”
Securities.”；第二段讲了一些公司在裁员甚至倒闭，“… interviews with more than a dozen industry participants suggest that firms large and small have been cutting staff, and in some cases have shut down.”。A 项，努力赚钱；B 项，股票交易市场的萎缩；C 项，利润和雇员人数的减少；D 项，不再活跃于全国股市。其中，A 项原文并未提及，B 项只提到了其中一种现象，比较片面，而 D 项说法过于绝对。故选 C 项。

items.stem: The phrase “swift reversal” most probably refers to ___ .

options.A: high – powered software and super – fast data connections
options.C: taking in charge of the price of a stock
options.D: not making huge profits as before

items.explanation: 语义理解题。题目意为：“swift reversal”这个词组很可能指的是 ___ 。A项，高性能软件和超高速数据连接；B项，成为营利机器的新投资者；C项，掌握股票价格；D项，没有像以前那样赚大钱。第三段“It is a swift reversal for trading firms that have often looked like profit machines in the eyes of other investors, thanks to high-powered software and super fast data connections that can take advantage of small changes in the price of a stock.”的意思是：这对于那些在其他投资者眼中经常看起来像营利机器的交易公司来说是一个迅速的逆转，因为它们过去利用高性能软件和超高速数据连接在股票价格的微小变化中获利。“swift reversal”在段落中主要是指来自市场的报复，即利润率的下降。故选D项。

items.stem: Which of the following would Peter Costa most probably agree on? ( )

options.A: Decline of high-speed firms is good for proper market functioning.
options.B: Traditional traders and investors are afraid of high-speed firms.
options.C: Stock markets need the presence of high-speed trading firms.
options.D: High-speed trading firms could bring order to stock markets.

items.explanation: 细节判断题。题目意为：Peter Costa 最有可能同意以下哪一项？Peter Costa 在文中所说的 “the fading presence of the firms could restore some order to stock markets”，其意思是：这些公司的逐渐衰落可能 “恢复股市的一些秩序”。A 项，高速公司的衰落有利于市场的正常运行；B 项，传统的交易者和投资者害怕高速公司；C 项，股市需要高速交易公司的存在；D 项，高速交易公司可以给股市带来秩序。故选 A 项。

items.source: 真题/【考试喵】2020年银保监会笔试真题及解析-财经岗.md
items.stem: Which of the following is TRUE according to the last paragraph? ( )

options.A: Regulators think the prospect of high-speed firms is promising.
options.B: The influence of the decline of high-speed firms is not certain.
options.C: The stock markets are under strong oversight.
options.D: The stock markets are confident to overcome the technical problems.

items.explanation: 细节理解题。题目意为：根据最后一段，下列哪一项是正确的？最后一段关键句“… it is hard to say how the decline of these firms will affect the markets.”，其意思是：很难说这些公司的衰落将如何影响市场。A项，监管者认为高速公司的前景是有希望的；B项，高速公司衰落的影响还不确定；C项，股市受到了强有力的监督；D项，股市有信心克服技术问题。其中，AD项的说法在原文均未提及，C项说法错误，只有B项符合文义。故选B项。

options.A: believe the world's environment is not as bad as it is thought to be
options.B: think the world's environment is in an undesirable condition
options.C: are not worried about the state of the world's environment

items.explanation:
细节理解题。题目意为：根据作者的说法，大多数学生 ___ 。其实是在问学生对于环境的认知。A 项，相信世界环境并没有想象中那么糟糕；B 项，认为世界环境不好；C 项，不担心世界环境状况；D 项，对环境有深刻的认识。根据第一段学生对于要讨
论的话题 “世界的环境非常健康” 的态度 “If that were an examination topic, most students would tear it apart, offering a long list of complaints: from local smog to global climate change, from the felling (砍伐) of forest to the extinction of species.” 可知，学生认为目前世界环境的状态并不好。故选 B 项。

options.A: has made the world's worse place to live in
options.B: has had a positive influence on the environment
options.C: has made the world an unpleasant place to live in
options.D: has not greatly affected the environment

items.explanation: 细节理解题。题目意为：世界人口和生产的巨大增长 ___ 。A 项，使世界变得更加不适宜居住；B 项，对环境产生了积极的影响；C 项，使世界成为一个令人居住得不愉快的地方；D 项，对环境影响不大。根据第二段 “Indeed, if people lived, consumed and produced things in the same way as they did in 1900 (or in 1950 or in 1980), the world by now would be a pretty disgusting place: smelly, dirty, toxic and dangerous.” 可知，按照 1900 年的生活方式，地球将会变得更臭、更脏、更危险，庞大的人口和生产量并没有极大地改变地球的环境。故选 D 项。

items.stem: One of the reasons why the long-term trend of prices has been downwards is that ___ .

options.C: new sources are always becoming available
options.D: new farming and crop technology can lead to overproduction

items.explanation: 细节理解题。题目意为：价格长期下跌的一个重要原因是 ___ 。A项，技术创新的出现；B项，消费将下降；C项，总可以找到新的来源；D项，新的农业和作物技术可能导致生产过剩。由第四段“What has happened is that every time a material seems to be running short, the price has risen and, in response, people have looked for new sources of supply, tried to find ways to use less of the material, or looked for a new substitute.”可知，每当一种材料要供不应求时，价格就会上涨，人们就会寻找新的供应来源，试图找到减少材料使用的方法，或者寻找新的替代品。故选C项。

items.stem: According to the author, why fish resources are diminishing? ( )

options.A: Because no new substitutes can be found available.
options.B: Because water pollution causes serious problems.
options.C: Because they are not owned by any particular entity.
options.D: Because fishing method is not sustainable.

items.explanation: 细节判断题。题目意为：根据作者所述，为什么鱼类资源正在减少？A项，因为找不到新的替代品；B项，因为水污染引起了严重的问题；C项，因为它们不属于任何特定实体；D项，因为捕鱼方法是不可持续的。由最后一段“If no one owns the resource concerned, no one has an interest in conserving it or fostering it: fish is the best example of this.”可知，作者认为鱼类资源不属于任何一类人，所以没有人会去关注，才导致鱼类资源的减少。故选C项。

items.stem: According to the author, the primary solution to environmental problems is ___ .

options.A: to allow market forces to operate property
options.B: to curb consumption of natural resources
options.C: to limit the growth of world population

items.explanation:

产品价格降低。故选 A 项。

High – speed trading firms—the lightning – quick, computerized companies that have risen in the last decade to dominate the nation's stock market—are now struggling to hold onto their gains. Profits from high – speed trading in American stocks are reported to be, at most, $1.25 billion this year, down 35 percent from last year and 74 percent from the peak of two years ago, according to estimates from the brokerage firm Rosenblatt Securities.
While no official data is available about the employment at the high – speed firms, interviews with more than a dozen industry participants suggest that firms large and small have been cutting staff, and in some cases have shut down. The firms also account for a declining percentage of a
shrinking pool of stock trading, from 61 percent three years ago to 51 percent now.
It is a swift reversal for trading firms that have often looked like profit machines in the eyes of other investors, thanks to high-powered software and super fast data connections that can take advantage of small changes in the price of a stock. High-speed trading is far from disappearing from the market, but the struggles facing these firms are welcomed by some traditional traders and investors who have viewed the firms as formidable rivals, or worse, market manipulators that create sudden increases and drops in share prices. Peter Costa, a long-time trader on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange, said the fading presence of the firms could “restore some order to stock markets”.
Regulators are still trying to understand whether the rise of high – speed firms has been a net benefit or loss for investors, so it is hard to say how the decline of these firms will affect the markets. Many market experts have argued that the technical problems that have recently hit the market have been a result of broader trend of the market turning into dozens of automated trading services and a lack of human oversight.

“The world’s environment is surprisingly healthy. Discuss.” If that were an examination topic, most students would tear it apart, offering a long list of complaints: from local smog to global climate change, from the felling (砍伐) of forest to the extinction of species. The list would largely be accurate, the concern legitimate. Yet the students who should be given the highest marks would actually be those who agreed with the statement. The surprise is how good things are, not how bad.
After all, the world’s population has more than tripled during this century, and world output has risen hugely, so you would expect the earth itself to have been affected. Indeed, if people lived, consumed and produced things in the same way as they did in 1900 (or in 1950 or in 1980), the world by now would be a pretty disgusting place: smelly, dirty, toxic and dangerous.
But they don’t. The reasons why they don’t, and why the environment has not been ruined, have to do with prices, technological innovation, social change and government regulation in response to popular pressure. That is why today’s environmental problems in the poor countries ought, in principle, to be solvable.
Raw materials have not run out, and show no sign of doing so. Logically, one day they must: the planet is a finite place. Yet it is also very big, and man is very ingenious. What has happened is that every time a material seems to be running short, the price has risen and, in response, people have looked for new sources of supply, tried to find ways to use less of the material, or looked for a new substitute. For this reason, prices for energy and for minerals have fallen in real terms.
during the century. The same is true for food. Prices fluctuate, in response to harvests, natural disasters and political instability, and when they rise, it takes some time before new sources of supply become available. But they always do, assisted by new farming and crop technology. The long-term trend has been downwards.
It is where prices and markets do not operate properly that this benign（良性的）trend begins to stumble, and the genuine problems arise. Markets cannot always keep the environment healthy. If no one owns the resource concerned, no one has an interest in conserving it or fostering it: fish is the best example of this.

“Sugar, alcohol and tobacco,” economist Adam Smith once wrote, “are commodities which are nowhere necessaries of life, which have become objects of almost universal consumption, and which are, therefore, extremely popular subjects of taxation.” Two and a half centuries on, most countries impose some sort of tax on alcohol and tobacco. With surging obesity（肥胖）level putting increasing strain on public health systems, governments around the world have begun to consider taxing sugars as well.
Whether such taxes work is still a matter of debate. A preliminary review of Mexico's taxation found a fall in purchases of taxed drinks as well as a rise in sales of un-taxed and healthier drinks. By contrast, a Danish tax on foods high in fats was abandoned a year after its introduction, amid claims that consumers were avoiding it by crossing the border to Germany to satisfy their desire for cheaper, fattier food.
The food industry, in general, firmly opposes the such direct government action. Nonetheless, the industry is under pressure to demonstrate its products are healthy as well as tasty. Over the past 30 years, the industry has made some efforts to improve the quality of its products. For example, some drink manufacturers have reduced the amount of sugar, salt or fat in a product, or found an alternative ingredient. More recently, however, some companies have been investing in a more ambitious undertaking: learning how to adjust the fundamental make – up of the food they sell. For example, having salt on the outside, but none on the inside, reduces the salt content without changing the taste.
While reformulating recipes is one way to improve public health, it should be a part of the multi-sided approach. The key is to remember that there is not just one solution. To deal with obesity, a mixture of approaches will be needed. There is no silver bullet.

Of all the lessons taught by the financial crisis, the most personal has been that we Americans should not be proud of our financial skills. We take out home loans we can't afford. We run up sky – high credit – card debts. We don't save nearly enough for retirement.
In response, supporters of financial – literacy education are raising their voices. School
districts in many states are adding money – management courses to their curriculum. The government is encouraging students to compete in the National Financial Capability Challenge. However, there is little evidence that traditional efforts to boost financial know–how help students make better decisions outside the classroom. Even as the financial–literacy movement has gained steam over the past decade, scores have been falling on tests that measure how well students perform in making financial decisions.
Given the situation, a growing number of researchers and educators agree that a more radical approach is needed. They advocate starting financial education a lot earlier than high school, putting real money and spending decisions into kids' hands, and encouraging students to talk openly about the emotions and social influences about spending.
Yet even the skeptics are slow to write off financial education completely. “We need to rigorously study the financial decisions of alumni like Ariel and Alex and compare with those of peers who didn’t get the same sort of education. Until you have experimental evidence, it is too speculative to recommend one education approach over another,” says Mike Sheden, a professor at Washington University in St. Louis who is conducting a seven-year study on whether giving children real bank accounts would result in long-term smart financial decisions. Yes, good, solid research like this takes a lot of time and resources, but it is in our own best interest to pursue it.
